title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Tuned continuous batching scheduler: improved fairness and starvation prevention across mixed-latency workloads, introduces adaptive request timeouts and queue-weight aging. No API changes.
description: Context: We observed tail-latency regressions and intermittent request starvation in the continuous-batcher under mixed short/long request workloads (embedding + long-context generation). This PR tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention heuristics, and introduce adaptive timeouts to reduce queue head-of-line blocking. Motivation: reduce P95/P99 latency for small requests without significantly degrading batch efficiency for long requests; avoid starvation of low-throughput tenants in multi-tenant GPU pools. Changes: 1) Introduces a queue-weight aging factor: requests gain priority the longer they wait (linear weight with caps) to prevent starvation of low-rate streams. 2) Changes batch selection from strict size-first to a weighted hybrid policy that balances batch fill vs. waiting-time to avoid starving short requests behind a stream of large long-running requests. 3) Adds adaptive per-request soft timeouts: if a request waits beyond adaptive_thresholds (based on recent service-time distributions) it is routed to a fast-path execution configuration (smaller batch/less KV-cache prefetch) or requeued with higher weight. 4) Adds metrics and tracing hooks: batch_wait_time, request_weight, preempt_count, adaptive_timeout_triggered, starvation_events; exposes them in runtime /metrics and Console dashboards. 5) Adds unit and integration tests, benchmark scripts, and docs. Risk and mitigation: changes are behind a runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler.v2 and default-off for Dedicated customers until gradual rollout. Observability added to validate behavior at canary scale before global rollout. Testing & benchmarks: local perf harness and simulated multi-tenant trace replay show P95 latency improvement for small requests by ~18% and P99 by ~12% at 40% throughput mix, with batch utilization drop <3%. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-3421 - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests against perf-canary harness - [x] CI green - [x] Metrics hooked - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Rollout doc updated (ops/continuous-batcher/rollout.md)

diff_snippet:
--- a/runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go
+++ b/runtime/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go
@@ -120,7 +120,28 @@ func chooseBatch(...) {
-    // previous size-first policy
-    return pickLargestReadyBatch()
+    // new weighted hybrid: combine wait-time weight with size score
+    // score = alpha*wait_weight + beta*size_score, alpha/beta configurable
+    // this prevents ongoing large requests from starving small ones
+    scores := computeScores(candidates)
+    return pickHighestScore(scores)
}
